text:
amanda: Heads up — CI microbench for PR #10021 just crossed the perf threshold on the kv-batching pipeline (tail latency jump). This was an otherwise small change to the batch window heuristic.
jiwoo: ugh. which test/metric? can you paste the failure snippet? :eyes:
amanda: From the CI output: 
```
CI microbench: kv_pipeline_latency_p99
baseline: 3.2 ms
PR-10021: 4.9 ms  (+53%)
threshold: 1.2x
```
also attaching the perf diff from the runner (small sample).
ci-bot: automated alert — perf-threshold-fail for pr/10021 on linux-x86-gpu1. Job: microbench-kv-pipeline. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/10021/logs
marco: Any recent kernel selector changes in that PR? PR said 'tweak window aligner' but didn't touch kernel selector explicitly.
amanda: No direct kernel changes but the heuristic now delays batch flush by up to 8ms for short seqs (intended to improve throughput). Looks like it changed batching distribution and triggered a slower kernel path in the runtime auto-selector.
sasha: Can you show a sample of the runtime logs when the failure happens? The selector usually emits a reason why it picked a kernel.
amanda: snippet from runtime.log when running the microbench: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:03:11Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel="matmul_fused" reason="default"
[2026-03-15T12:03:11Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel="matmul_v2" reason="seq_len>64 && batch_wait>5ms"
[2026-03-15T12:03:11Z] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.12
[2026-03-15T12:03:11Z] batcher: batch_size=2 wait=7.6ms
```
marco: there — matmul_v2 is slower for our model shape but the selector thinks it's better for longer sequences. The new batching delay is pushing more short requests into the 'batch_wait>5ms' condition so it flips kernel.
jiwoo: Could be two orthogonal regressions: changed batching increases wait times -> selector picks different kernel -> slower path. Did we see KV cache hit rate drop too? That log shows 12% hit. Baseline typically ~40% for these tests.
amada: (typo: amanda) baseline kv hit in golden run was 38%. After PR: 11-14%. So both things changed.
sasha: That explains it. Longer batch wait plus lower kv-hit means more decoder tokens computed wasted, hurting p99. We should reproduce locally with the same microbench harness.
marco: I'll try a two-point bisect: revert the batching change and run microbench; then revert kernel selector tuning if needed. Which commit in PR touches the aligner? commit c3f8a2.
jiwoo: If local repro is fast, we can try a hotfix: reduce the max wait from 8ms to 4ms in the heuristic, then re-run CI. If that restores kernel choice and kv-hit, it's a good candidate.
amanda: Repro steps I used: 
```
./scripts/run_microbench --test kv_pipeline --model redwood-l1 --iters 1000 --seq 64 --host linux-x86-gpu1
```
I'll run baseline vs PR head now and paste logs.
ci-bot: job queued (microbench/10021/repro). ETA ~12m.
(dev-bot reaction): :hourglass_flowing_sand: queued
marco: FYI I profiled a quick run and uploaded a flamegraph: https://perf-internal/graphs/10021/flame.svg. The hot path shows an unexpected matmul_v2 kernel hot spot and increased memcpy around KV eviction.
sasha: That suggests eviction churn too. Lower kv hit might be due to slightly different batching aligning different prefixes and populating cache differently.
jiwoo: Two-action plan: 1) revert batching wait heuristic in PR to verify perf fix; 2) add a protected gate in the runtime selector so the kernel flip requires both seq_len and stable batch distribution (avoid flipping on transient waiting spikes). Which do we want as short-term?
amanda: Revert first. I'll open a revert PR now and tag this thread. If revert fixes CI we can discuss longer-term change.
marco: Also add a test that asserts kernel selection stability given same trace distribution — maybe a microbench that runs many small sequences and checks chosen kernel histogram.
sasha: Agreed. Without that we'll keep flipping.
jiwoo: ok, amanda — once you open revert PR, ping @eng-runtime and I'll queue a canary run on dedicated infra.
amanda: Revert created: PR #10024 — revert commit c3f8a2 from #10021. Kicking CI.
ci-bot: PR #10024 build started. microbench job scheduled.
(10m later) ci-bot: microbench job completed. result: pass — kv_pipeline_latency_p99 = 3.1 ms (within baseline).
amanda: Looks like revert fixes it.
marco: Good. I'll follow up with a smaller heuristic tweak that keeps low-latency flows out of the wait path and add a regression test for kernel selection and kv-hit distribution.
sasha: Also add a log metric for "batcher: wait_histogram" so CI perf can detect distribution shifts rather than only p99.
jiwoo: Nice. Thanks everyone — let's not roll the original change until we have selector guardrails and tests. :thumbsup:
amanda: filing follow-ups: issue #2482 (selector guardrail) and #2483 (batcher wait metric + regression test).
